context: Arc diagram showing co-occurrence relationships among 30 characters from a synthetic novel, with nodes ordered by first appearance along a baseline and ~90 quadratic bezier arcs above encoding co-occurrence weight via height and stroke width. A 9-color Tol muted palette maps arc color to the earlier character's first chapter. Hover dims unconnected arcs; a brush on the chapter axis filters edges by co-occurrence chapter range.
first_impression: In the default (no-hover) state the middle section reads as a moderate tangle — individual arcs are hard to trace and the 9-color palette at 0.35 opacity blends into an indistinct haze, but the overall shape of the network (dense early characters, sparse late ones) is legible.
what_works: The hover interaction is well-calibrated — dimming non-neighbors to 0.04 opacity immediately isolates a character's connections with minimal transition lag (120ms), which is the primary mechanism that makes this diagram usable. Arc height scaling via scaleSqrt and stroke width together provide two redundant weight cues that hold up even under density.
what_doesnt: Nine categorical hues at 35% opacity over overlapping arcs causes simultaneous color collisions throughout the middle of the diagram — the color encoding (first chapter of the earlier character) is not explained by any legend and is effectively unreadable in the default view. The chapter brush axis shares the same pixel range as the node x-axis but uses a different spatial logic (linear chapters vs. point-scale sort order), creating a subtle misalignment that makes brushed regions feel loosely coupled to the nodes they dim.
